title: Subtract what you cannot measure
question: Which difference survives when the accounts are subtracted?
recap: Subtracting the energy losses gives L(γ − 1), without choosing the body’s internal energy.
premises: Both energy balances describe the same emission.
limitations: Calling the remaining difference kinetic energy requires the next premise.

overview.text: Subtract the rest-account loss from the traveler’s loss. The difference is 2.5 units in the large-number example. We still have not opened the boxes containing the body’s unknown energies.

full.text: Subtract the rest-frame balance from the moving-frame balance and regroup the terms. The first bracket compares the two accounts before emission; the second compares them afterward.

full.spoken: The before frame-energy difference minus the after frame-energy difference equals L times gamma minus one.

full.text: This step needs no value for the absolute internal energy. It is an algebraic consequence of the two balances. It has not yet established that the surviving quantity is the change in energy of motion: that identification needs a physical premise.

items: Start with H₀ − H₁ = γL and E₀ − E₁ = L.
Subtract the second equation from the first: H₀ − H₁ − E₀ + E₁ = γL − L.
Regroup the left as (H₀ − E₀) − (H₁ − E₁).
Factor L on the right to obtain L(γ − 1).
Keep the result as a difference between accounts until the relation to energy of motion has been stated.

margin.text: A cancellation does not prove that the terms have the physical interpretation we would like. Keeping the algebraic subtraction separate from its kinetic interpretation makes a changed premise testable in the two-ledgers laboratory.
